people.x: Unnamed Northern Wei emperor after Yong'an; chapter gives only the title 魏帝
Unnamed father entailed as son of Han Jing and father of Han Xiong
Biography subject of Wei Xuan continued from the prior chunk; owned units name him as 玄/Xuan or by silent subject.

claims.statement: Elder brother, wife, and children were captured together; children unnamed and uncounted (妻子).

claims.cause: city fell when attacked by Hou Jing

label.en: posthumous Grand Commandant and related honors
Executive Commissioner of the Capital South

claims.action: defeated Murong Shaozong and beheaded Xue Xi
escorted fleeing princes and officials to Guanzhong
reinforced Li Yansun and fought through to Fulu
ambushed Eastern Wei grain convoy and died

claims.statement: stray arrow struck neck and exited through mouth; temporarily lifeless

claims.action: fought forty-five battles on the frontier

claims.assessment: excelled at generosity and winning troops hearts; weaker than Han Xiong at archery
excelled at strong-bow archery; weaker than Chen Xin at winning troops by largesse

claims.action: returned south of passes prioritizing loyalty over retrieving mother and brother

label.en: posthumous Equal to Three Dukes and Governor of Qi
posthumous Equal to Three Dukes and Governor of Xu

claims.action: received Gao Zhongmi and fought at Mount Mang

label.en: fief of nine hundred households in all
Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office

claims.outcome: withdrew; suffered dozens killed or wounded and lost horses, armor, and spears
killed and wounded dozens; captured horses, armor, and spears; Yongye withdrew

claims.assessment: His rule was simple and generous, and the people were content
endowed with courage and stratagem; entrusted with defense of frontier fortresses
in repelling invasion stood equal to heroes of earlier ages; helped hold the Yi and Luo and Xiao and Han, blunting Qi designs and easing Zhou eastern concerns
among the several generals whose strength held the Yi and Luo and eased Zhou concern for the east

translationRepairs: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor, commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander-in-chief over military affairs in twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and governor of Ding province.

In the first year of Datong he was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander-in-chief over military affairs in twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and governor of Ding province.
s0019 has 追贈太尉; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, whereas Grand Mentor is 太傅, so the replacement corrects a real title error.

In the first year of Datong he was posthumously awarded Grand Mentor, commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander over the military affairs of the twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and Governor of Ding Province.

In the first year of Datong he was posthumously awarded Grand Commandant, commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander over the military affairs of the twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and Governor of Ding Province.
Literal of s0019 likewise renders 太尉 wrongly as Grand Mentor; Grand Commandant matches the Chinese office.
His grandfather Bofu distinguished himself in the late Taihe campaigns against Xuanchi and was appointed administrator of Runan commandery.
His grandfather Bofu distinguished himself in the late Taihe campaigns against Xuanhu and was appointed administrator of Runan commandery.
s0003 has 從征懸瓠; 懸瓠 is the place Xuanhu, not Xuanchi, so the naming repair is required.
His grandfather Bofu, at the end of the Taihe era of Wei, followed the campaign against Xuanchi with merit and became Administrator of Runan Commandery.
His grandfather Bofu, at the end of the Taihe era of Wei, followed the campaign against Xuanhu with merit and became Administrator of Runan Commandery.
Literal of s0003 has the same 懸瓠; Xuanhu is the accurate English form and Xuanchi is wrong.
[xian [in the received text]] duke, with a fief increased by one thousand households.
county duke, with a fief increased by one thousand households.
s0209 reads 〔縣〕公 after 許昌 in s0207; the idiomatic field wrongly keeps editorial apparatus instead of rendering 縣公 as county duke.
When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to earl, and his fief was increased to nine hundred households in all with what came before.
When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Xuan's rank was advanced to earl, and his fief was increased to nine hundred households in all with what came before.
s0214's silent subject continues Wei Xuan's biography (進爵為伯); after 孝閔帝踐阼, bare 'his' wrongly suggests the emperor was enfeoffed, and naming Xuan matches the idiomatic field and context.
In the fourth year he was made General of Agile Cavalry with a baron's establishment equal to the Three Dukes and moved his garrison to Yanhan.
In the fourth year he was made General of Agile Cavalry and Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office, and moved his garrison to Yanhan.
s0216 has 開府儀同三司, the Kaifu Yitong Sansi honor; 'baron's establishment' invents a noble fief reading of 開府 and must be replaced.
In the fourth year he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes, and transferred his garrison to Yanhan.
In the fourth year he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office, and transferred his garrison to Yanhan.
Literal of s0216 likewise mistranslates 開府儀同三司 as a baronial establishment; Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office is the correct honorific.

[zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan with Yuwenneng, Zhao Gan, and five hundred foot and horse south of Lulu Crossing to ambush Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.

[zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan with Yitong Yuwen Neng, Zhao Gan, and five hundred foot and horse south of Lulu Crossing to ambush Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.
s0220 has 儀同宇文能; 儀同 is the Yitong rank and 宇文能 is Yuwen Neng, so fused 'Yuwenneng' without the office is wrong.

[zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan leading Yuwenneng, Baron with an establishment, Zhao Gan, and others with five hundred infantry and cavalry south of Lulu Crossing to intercept and strike Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.

[zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan leading Yitong Yuwen Neng, Zhao Gan, and others with five hundred infantry and cavalry south of Lulu Crossing to intercept and strike Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.
Literal of s0220 wrongly turns 儀同 into 'Baron with an establishment' and fuses 宇文能; Yitong Yuwen Neng restores both office and name spacing.

By this they were able to display arms at the Yi and Luo, hold and secure Xiao and Han, make the men of Qi frustrate their plan of advancing west, and ease the Zhou court's concern of looking east—all through the power of these several generals.

By this they were able to display arms at the Yi and Luo, hold and secure Xiao and Han, frustrate the men of Qi in their plan of advancing west, and ease the Zhou court's concern of looking east—all through the power of these several generals.
s0199 has 齊人沮西略之謀; 沮 marks the Qi western plan as frustrated by the Zhou generals, not Qi men frustrating their own plan.
